venue.name: Quw'utsun Syuw'entst Lelum' Culture and Education Centre
venue.description: Quw'utsun Syuw'entst Lelum', which the site translates as Cowichan teachings house, is the Culture and Education department of Cowichan Tribes, at 5744 Allenby Road in Duncan. Its own page says it promotes the understanding of Cowichan culture and language to both the First Nation and non-First Nation community, and provides educational support to Cowichan Tribes members. It runs the Nation's daycare, elementary school, adult learning centre and language classes, and sells Hul'q'umi'num' books, posters, flashcards and DVDs from its building. Nowhere on the Cowichan Tribes website are there opening hours, admission prices, tours or any offering for a visiting school or daycare group, and the building at 200 Cowichan Way that once held the Quw'utsun' Cultural and Conference Centre is now published as the address of the Kwun'atsustul counselling service.

gaps: OPERATING STATUS: the Cowichan Tribes website has no page for a public cultural centre. A search of their own site for 'cultural centre', 'Quw'utsun Cultural', 'Cultural and Education Centre', 'field trip' and 'tours' returns nothing that a visitor could book. The name that does appear is Quw'utsun Syuw'entst Lelum', described on their own pages as the Nation's Education and Culture department, which is what this record covers.

The old Quw'utsun' Cultural and Conference Centre at 200 Cowichan Way appears on the Cowichan Tribes site only twice: once in a councillor's biography as a place she used to work, and once as the current address of the Kwun'atsustul counselling service. On the operator's own site there is no sign it still runs as a place the public can visit.
No opening hours, admission price, tour, workshop or school program is published, so the programs list is empty. That is because nothing is offered on the site, not because a page failed to load.

Whether the department will host or visit an outside school or daycare group is simply not addressed anywhere on the site, so nothing was recorded either way. A director who wants a Hul'q'umi'num' language or Cowichan culture session would have to phone the education office and ask.
No street level detail at all is published for visitors: no washrooms, no lunch space, no step free access, no parking, no room for a bus.

Language and culture resources are listed for sale at the Quw'utsun Syuw'entst building with prices ranging from $10 for a video to $80 for a set of six books. Those are shop prices for materials, not the cost of a visit.
No usable photograph was found. The only image on the department's pages is the Cowichan Tribes logo, so the images list is empty and there is no hero image.
No coordinates are published and no geocoding service was available in this run, so the address is recorded and the coordinates are left to be filled in later.

The site's own copyright line still reads 2021, and several linked forms are dated 2022, so parts of these pages have not been updated in some years. The news and newsletter sections are current to 2026.
